questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The choice of destination was based on the academic opportunities of the university, both with regard to the academic level of the courses offered, the professors teaching the courses, the availability of courses of interest to me, as well as the overall academic level of the university and its students. I therefore chose to go to New York University School of Law.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Somewhat difficult. NYU Law only takes in a handful of exchange students every semester, and their main focus is on the LLM-students and JD-students. While this is very reasonable, it does make it more difficult for an exchange student to find the necessary information that does not already apply to LLM-students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: NYU Law has a great administration handling everything relating to international students; both exchange students and LLM-students. Once the semester started (a few weeks after arrival and upon completion of the introduction course), the people of the exchange office were both very helpful and very nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy. I used Alohause, a platform for short term leases. I found a four bedroom apartment in Bushwick alongside three Danes. We ended up becoming great friends.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The cost is still very high. But it is a great opportunity to not have the entire semester revolving around NYU Law - when you live off campus, it is much easier to go explore other parts of the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At NYU Law, you make bids for every course that you would like to have. Each student is awarded 1000 points, and over a certain period of time the initial bids have to be made. Then, in the first few weeks after the courses have started, students are able to drop courses and join other courses that have not already been filled up. One of the upsides of this system is that if the individual student is really eager to be enrolled in a certain course, that student can choose to make a high bid for that course, thereby overbidding the other bidders. Each student is able to make its own determination with regard to the courses that the student would like, and taking into account the available information on previous years' bidding cycles, the students are well equipped to make proper bids for the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A guide before entering the initial bids. Once we got to NYU Law, the people of the course registration office were of great help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite successful, getting most of the courses I wanted. I was able to rearrange my entire course registration in the later bidding cycle.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: For every semester, students are asked to review their classes, both with regard to overall experience, course work load and the professors teaching styles. I did not know of this information before registrating for classes, but it would have been of great help for me to understand the individual course better.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took law school courses offered to 2Ls and LLM-students. Naturally, they were all graduate/MA level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more interaction with the students, and the professors were very well prepared. The course work load was fine, much like in UCPH. But the students were better prepared for the individual class, and the law school had mandatory attendance.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to US Law.
Investment Treaty Arbitration
International Commercial Arbitration
Contracts (for LLM students)
International Arbitration and the CISG
Cross-Border Mergers and Acquisitions.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. For each course, the professor was very well prepared, skilled, friendly and passionate. I would like to also note that taking courses specifically on US law is very interesting as an exchange student.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Registration fees incurred doing the formal process of getting accepted at NYU Law.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing is more expensive than I thought, and every day expenses (coffee, lunch, etc.) is also very expensive as you have to include a 20 % tip.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We had boat parties, social gatherings, LLM/Exchange student events, sport activities, tickets to broadway and so much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go for a run in Central Park, alongside the Hudson, and in Prospect Park. Also, take the subway to a random location and walk through the neighborhood. NYC has so much to offer, and it would be a shame to spend all of it in the library or in your apartment. Go for the sunday bottomless brunch, go to that flea market with some fellow students, arrange a movie night at Dumbo Park and have the NYC Skyline as a magnificent backdrop. You will not regret doing all of those things instead of studying your semester away. You have time for both - and then some.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Philadelphia, go do a weekend hike upstate. Go to the food market in Queens, go to Washington and Boston. With public transportation, these places are max. 3 hours away.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. NYC is an international metropolitan, and so it is easy to mix in with the "locals".

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Talking to strangers and tipping.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of New Yorkers. People are much more eager to talk to each other than we are in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to make friends with the LLM-students. They are just as new in the city as you are, and even though they are often older and more experienced, they also came to have a great time. 

Get a sense of your neighborhood, and explore the city! It is so diverse that you will never get bored of it. 

Be active in class. It is much more normal than back home at UCPH, and it is a great experience when you get familiar with the course topics, your class mates and professors.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Both the social and the academic experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being active in class / getting called on. Bot you quickly get used to it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
